stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist's personal registration expired 61 days ago. It has never been suspended or revoked. The pharmacist pays the renewal and late fees this morning and asks to begin a shift while the Board processes the renewal. Which statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The pharmacist falls within the 60-day fee-only branch and may practice once payment is submitted.
Any lapse beyond 60 days automatically requires passage of the MPJE before renewal.
Direct oversight by another pharmacist permits practice until the registration is renewed.
Board conditions may apply, but the over-two-year MPJE branch does not; practice must wait for renewal.
The registration remains effective for six months after expiration if all continuing education was completed on time.

explanation.core_reasoning: A 61-day lapse is more than 60 days but far less than two years. It therefore enters the branch in which the Board may impose renewal conditions, which may include additional continuing education. The express MPJE requirement belongs to a lapse exceeding two years. Because practice after expiration is unlicensed practice, submitting fees does not authorize the pharmacist to work before renewal.

choice_analysis.A: Sixty-one days is outside the branch that ends at 60 days, and filing payment is not itself renewal.
choice_analysis.B: The express MPJE requirement is tied to a lapse exceeding two years, not merely 60 days.
choice_analysis.C: Another pharmacist's oversight does not restore an expired personal registration.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the 61-day duration activates possible Board conditions, not the over-two-year MPJE rule, and practice must await renewal.
choice_analysis.E: Timely continuing education does not create a six-month practice grace period after registration expiration.

related_facts: Personal pharmacist registrations expire on December 31 of each even-numbered year unless timely renewed.
A lapse exceeding two years requires passage of the MPJE in addition to satisfaction of other Board conditions.
explanation.mpje_trap: The 60-day and two-year thresholds govern different consequences; crossing the first does not import the express condition attached to the second.

reasoning_steps: Classify 61 days as more than 60 days
Confirm that 61 days does not exceed two years
Apply possible Board conditions without importing the over-two-year MPJE requirement
Require completed renewal before practice resumes
